newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Tuan Sing may get land in China lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Tuan Sing may get land in China lawsuit.

text.p: Diversified property company Tuan Sing could get land in China in compensation for winning a law suit over a failed Chinese property deal, chief executive officer and managing director Hwang Soo Chin said on Monday.
Tuan Sing said in June its unit Shanghai T.S. International Real Estate Co Ltd had won a Singapore $10 million lawsuit against Shanghai Shuang Lu Real Estate Management Co Ltd.
The Shanghai High Court had also ruled that a third party, Shanghai County Real Estate General Company, was also liable.
The company said previously this meant that if Tuan Sing's subsidiary was unable to enforce the judgment against Shanghai Shuang Lu, it could proceed to enforce the judgment against the third party.
Hwang told reporters after the ceremony for a new property project that the defendant had appealed but the Appeal Court had upheld the judgment.
He said the case had gone to the Execution Court, where all parties could be called to settle the case amicably.
"We are not so much hopeful of getting cash. We are hoping to get compensation in kind -- in the form of land," he said.
"We have to sit down and discuss what sort of land is available, whether it suits our purpose. At the end of the day, we have to put a value on the land...," he said.
He expected the land to be located in Yin Chun residential area in Shanghai's Min Hang district for local housing -- the same area where the original property deal to acquire a site failed.
Tuan Sing had already made provision for about S$10 million in its books for the year ending December 1996. Hwang said any compensation would be a bonus.
